subtitle: Active roster on September 30, 2026: 40 players. 21 position players included, 19 pitchers excluded. Regular season ended September 27 (28 active that day). September is regular-season games from September 1–30. Last 10 is each hitter’s last 10 games with a plate appearance on or before September 30.
footnote1: Archetype picks the contact-quality rate shown on both rows for that hitter. Damage rate is the share of tracked fair batted balls with exit velocity greater than 95 mph and launch angle of at least 10 degrees. Tracked fair batted balls are Statcast pitches with type X and non-null exit velocity and launch angle. Barrel rate is Statcast barrel% (launch_speed_angle = 6) on that same denominator. The default rule uses 2026 regular-season competitive contact, which is those batted balls excluding bunts. Average exit velocity is the mean on competitive contact. A hitter is Barrel only when that average is at least 1.0 mph below the pooled MLB average and the barrel rate is a standout relative to exit velocity: at least 2.0 percentage points above the barrel rate predicted from average EV. The prediction is an ordinary-least-squares line fit to every 2026 MLB hitter with at least 100 competitive batted balls (n=406 hitters): predicted barrel% = -79.37 + 0.99 × (avg EV in mph), R² = 0.567. Everyone else with enough data is Damage. That covers average-or-better exit velocity (a real-power profile) and a clearly low exit velocity whose barrel rate is not above the exit-velocity prediction by the standout gap. Hitters with fewer than 20 competitive batted balls stay unclassified and the contact cells are blank. Overrides, applied after the rule: Brooks Lee is Damage, and Luke Keaschall is Barrel. The superscript 1 sits on Keaschall’s archetype. 2026 MLB average EV on competitive contact was 88.0 mph (n=124,098). 2026 MLB barrel rate was 7.7% (n=124,098 tracked batted balls, bunts included in that denominator). Brooks Lee’s 2026 competitive-contact average EV was 87.8 mph (n=488) and his barrel rate was 4.5%. avg EV 87.8 is not at least 1.0 mph below league 88.0 (real-power / not-clearly-below screen) Final label: Damage. Luke Keaschall’s 2026 competitive-contact average EV was 84.8 mph (n=450) and his barrel rate was 3.8%. avg EV 84.8 is below league 88.0, but barrel% 3.8 is only -0.9 points versus the EV prediction of 4.7% (standout requires +2.0 points) Final label: Barrel.
footnote2: Execution uses three equally weighted inputs. Each rate is divided by the MLB pooled league rate for the same definition, the three ratios are averaged, and the result is multiplied by 100. Composite = 100 × ((RISP knock-in / league RISP knock-in) + (move-over / league move-over) + (QAB / league QAB)) / 3. A composite of 100 is league average. The raw rates are not averaged together, because they sit on different scales. RISP knock-in is the share of plate appearances that begin with a runner on second and/or third in which the batter is credited with at least one RBI (MLB Stats API result.rbi on that plate appearance). Move-over denominator: plate appearances that begin with a runner on second, nobody on third, and 0 outs. A runner on first is allowed. Base-out state is the first tracked pitch of the plate appearance. Success: the runner who began the plate appearance on second has an end-of-PA state of safe at third (API movement end 3B) or safe at home (end score). He is not successful if he is out, if he never leaves second, or if he only touches third and is then retired. Advancement on the batted ball, a walk, hit-by-pitch, wild pitch, passed ball, balk, or stolen base during the plate appearance all count. A strikeout on which that runner does not end safe at third or home is a failure. QAB is the share of plate appearances with more than 5 pitches (6 or more Statcast pitches). September rows use September 1–30, 2026 MLB rates. Last-10 rows use full-season 2026 MLB rates, because those games are not one shared month. 2026 MLB RISP knock-in rate was 24.2% (n=43,715 PA). 2026 MLB 0-out, second-to-third move-over rate was 56.2% (n=5,629 PA). 2026 MLB QAB rate (more than 5 pitches) was 20.6% (n=183,849 PA). September 2026 MLB RISP knock-in rate was 25.0% (n=6,463). September move-over rate was 55.8% (n=847). September QAB rate was 21.0% (n=27,294). Also indexed the same way: 2026 barrel% 7.7%, damage rate 22.1%, in-zone whiff 13.9%, chase 30.3%. September barrel% 7.7%, damage rate 21.9%, in-zone whiff 14.2%, chase 30.4%.
color_note: White band is within 10% of the comparison league rate, inclusive (ratio 0.90 to 1.10). For the composite, that is 90 to 110. Small sample: under 8 tracked batted balls for contact quality; under 10 in-zone swings, out-of-zone pitches, or plate appearances for whiff, chase, RISP knock-in, move-over, and QAB. The execution composite is uncolored when the window has under 10 plate appearances. A composite can be colored while its move-over or RISP cell stays gray, because those splits are rarer than a month of plate appearances. Santurce hitter cards color a continuous blue-to-red magnitude scale (rateHeatStyle in pregame.html). This sheet uses the requested direction instead: white at the league band, green when the rate is better, red when it is worse. Header navy #122C6F matches the Santurce licey navy. Cell green and red are light fills so the numbers stay readable; they are not the Santurce magnitude gradient.
roster_note: MLB Stats API active roster for the Twins on 2026-09-30 listed 40 players (21 position players, 19 pitchers). The active roster on 2026-09-27, the last day with regular-season games, listed 28 players (15 position players). September call-ups and postseason recalls are whoever the active endpoint listed on Sept 30; pitchers are excluded. Last-10 games can predate September when that is when the hitter last played.
coverage_note: Schedule finals: 2,429 regular-season games, 2026-03-25 through 2026-09-27. Statcast covered 2,429 of those game pks (100.0%). Plate appearances: 183,849. API join on game and at-bat (Statcast at_bat_number = API atBatIndex + 1, same batter): 100.0%. Batter-id mismatches: 0.
sources_note: Roster, schedule, transactions, RBI, and runner movement: MLB Stats API (statsapi.mlb.com), public endpoints, no login. Pitches, zones, swing descriptions, exit velocity, launch angle, and the barrel flag (launch_speed_angle = 6): Baseball Savant Statcast, downloaded with pybaseball and cached under /Users/colbymorris/twins-hitter-sheet/cache/statcast. Play-by-play extracts cached under /Users/colbymorris/twins-hitter-sheet/cache/pbp. Regular season only (schedule gameType=R and Statcast game_type=R).
blank_note: Cells are blank when the denominator is zero or, for the composite, when any of the three input rates is undefined. Archetype contact cells are blank when the hitter has fewer than 20 competitive batted balls and is not Brooks Lee or Luke Keaschall. No rate was imputed from a nearby player, from a career norm, or from memory.
